full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 29-4-2014 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Mymensingh in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 07 of 2009 affirming the judgment and order dated 20-1-2009 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Mymensingh in House Rent Case No. 55 of 2011 should not be set-aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Facts in short are that the petitioner as petitioner submitted a petition under section 19(1) of the Premises Rent Control Act which was registered as House Rent Case No. 55 of 2001 in the first court of Senior Assistant Judge, Mymensingh for depositing rent of the disputed premises. 

 4. The opposite-parties entered appearance in the above case and submitted a written objection. It was stated that the petitioner, a tenant under the opposite-parties paid rent for the month of Falgun, 1407 BS for the disputed premises. But he did not pay any rent for the subsequent months. Since the petitioner is a defaulter in paying rent of the disputed premises and the opposite-parties has filed a case for eviction of the petitioner. 

 5. On consideration of facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record the learned Senior Assistant Judge rejected the case and refused to receive the rent of the disputed premises. 

 6. Being aggrieved by above judgment and order of the learned Assistant Judge opposite-parties preferied miscellaneous appeal No. 07 of 2009 to the District Judge, Mymensingh which was transferred to the Court of Joint District Judge, Second Court for hearing and disposal. 

 8. Being aggrieved by the above judgment and order of the learned additional District Judge the appellant as petitioner has preferred this civil revision case and obtained this Rule. 

 9. None appears on behalf of the petitioner when the case was taken up for hearing. 

 10. Mr Md Golam Rabbani learned Advocate for the opposite-parties submits that the petitioner is a habitual defaulter in paying rent of the disputed premises. The opposite-parties has filed a case for eviction of the opposite-parties from the disputed premises. As such the learned Senior Assistant Judge rightly dismissed the House Rent Case of the petitioner the learned Joint District Judge rightly dismissed the Appeal and affirmed the judgment and order of the learned Assistant Judge which calls for no interference. 

 12. At the very outset it needs to be mentioned that the learned Senior Assistant Judge who is also an ex-officio rent controller by virtue of his position committed an error illegality in registering the petition of the petitioner under section 19 of the Premises Rent Control Act as a miscellaneous case and receiving evidence and pronouncing a judgment on the matter in his judicial capacity. The Premises Rent Control Act does not create a separate office for the rent controller nor appointed any person exclusively to that position. But all the Senior Assistant Judges and Joint District Judges are appointed ex-officio rent controller for the respective area of their territorial jurisdiction. A senior Assistant Judge is a rent controller in the area of his territorial jurisdiction but while acting as a rent controller he is not a civil judge. 

 13. It is well settled that the Rent Controller is not a court but a mere candor pipe for receiving rent from the tenant for the landlord who is at liberty to withdraw the same at any time. The Rent Controller does not have any judicial power to entertain any case or receive evidence or make a judicial determination. But surprisingly in this case the Rent Controller of Mymensingh entertained a judicial proceeding, recorded evidence and gave a decision which was appealed in the form of a Miscellaneous Appeal to the Court of District Judge, Mymensingh. 

 16. But the Rent Controller erroneously assumed judicial power and converted above petition into a miscellaneous case and refused to deposit or receive rent from the petitioner which were all illegal and completely without jurisdiction. 

 17. Similarly the learned Joint District Judge without proper appreciation of facts and laws involved in the matter most illegally entertained a Miscellaneous appeal against the order of the rent controller, and by the impugned judgment and order unlawfully affirmed above illegal order of the rent controller which is not tenable in law. 

 18. This Court finds merit in the instant Civil Revision Case and the Rule deserves to be made absolute. 

 20. The judgment and order dated 29-6-2014 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Mymensingh in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 07 of 2009 affirming that of the learned Senior Assistant Judge dated 20-1-2009 is hereby set-aside. The Rent Controller, Mymensingh is hereby directed to receive rent from the petitioner and deposit the same for the opposite-parties.
